featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to this restaurant with my friend. The place was empty on a Saturday evening, which should have been the first red flag. We ordered Veg kolhapuri, cheese naan and  Korean rice. The naan was undercooked and the dough was still raw inside. When the KOREAN RICE arrived it tasted like veg fried rice with Manchurian. Absolutely underwhelming. After 2 spoons I bite into something which almost broken off my teeth. It was a rock bigger than 1 cm. No exaggeration. I called over the waiter and showed him the rock. They offered to change the dish but how can you trust a place after they've served you food with big rock in it which almost broke my tooth. I don't know how did the chef not notice such a big rock while preparing the food, it's impossible to miss while cooking.
Oh and no regret/remorse/apology from the owner/cashier. Simply "Madam dish change kardu kya" from a waiter. How is this place still open. Is there no food inspection? They should be shut down.

featured_reviews.review_text: Sahibaan is a popular restaurant located in Colaba. The food here is simply amazing. featured_reviews.review_text:

It's priced moderately high.

featured_reviews.name: Anagha Nair
featured_reviews.review_text:
So we recently went to this restaurant in the evening.The resturant wasn't that busy and we could peacefully enjoy our food.

Sahibaan Oriental and Indian Resturant is a restaurant located in the heart of Colaba. It is a popular one for both locals and tourists.

The food is consistently good, with dishes that are flavorful. Portion sizes are generous, and the presentation is also appealing.

I would not recommend the sizzling Ice cream brownie from here,it was rather too hot and the brownie was not up to the mark.

The service staff were attentive and professional.
If you are looking for a special occasion restaurant in Mumbai, Then this is an good option.

Note:-As the serving portion of our spring roll was large we asked the waiter to pack it up,but forgot to pick it up when paying the bill.Please do not do this mistake as we did. If anyone wishes to parcel the food they didn't finish,remind them during bill payment.

Here is the list of food we ordered:-
Chicken Spring Roll
Chicken Lollipop
Pot Noodles
Sizzling Ice Cream Brownie

Overall, I would highly recommend The Sahibaan Oriental and Indian Resturant to anyone looking for a great dining experience in Colaba. It is a bit on the expensive side, but the quality of the food, service, and atmosphere is worth it.

Second time went there on 15 August 2024 suffered from severe food poisoning. Never going back here.

I visited Jia The Oriental Kitchen and had a really great experience.
The ambience is beautiful, calm and very classy.

We started with Lychee & Jasmine Fizz and Sakura Cooler both were refreshing.
The Chicken Yakitori was smoky and juicy.
The Sui Mai dumplings were soft and flavourful.

The Prawn Thai curry with jasmine rice was my favourite dish.

featured_reviews.review_text:

The mushroom dumpling in chilli oil was bursting with flavor and had just the right amount of spice. The crispy asparagus tempura roll was beautifully done — light, fresh, and perfectly crunchy.

featured_reviews.review_text: BEWARE: PORTION SIZES ARE BIG. we had the Peking Duck shown as a small starter size as you can see by the photo. Service was great as there were many staff. Prices are reasonable for location, choice and food quality.

featured_reviews.name: Veeni Saumil Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for Asian food in Colaba, Jia Oriental is a place worth visiting. The moment you step in, the ambience sets the tone... calm, modern, and elegant, making it ideal for a relaxed lunch or dinner.
We began with the Lychee & Jasmine Fizz, which was light, floral, and refreshing.
The Manchow soup that followed was comforting, flavourful, and well balanced.
One of my favourites from the meal was the pan-fried mushroom bao.. soft, juicy, and packed with umami flavours.
The Vegetable Dragon Roll, Signature Sushi, was equally enjoyable, with crispy vegetables and creamy avocado creating a nice balance of textures and taste.
The rice and noodles were simple and satisfying, complementing the rest of the dishes well.
A standout and something a little different was the Mushroom Chung Fung.. delicately steamed, silky in texture, and definitely a must-try if you enjoy subtle, comforting flavours.
We ended the meal with the Pull Me Up cake, which truly completed the experience. Rich, indulgent, and a perfect sweet finish.

Overall, Jia Oriental offers a lovely combination of good food, elegant ambience, and a relaxed dining experience. A great option in Colaba for anyone craving Asian flavours, sushi, and dim sums in a comfortable, well-designed setting.

Starters were fried corn curd- like a sweet corn soup but in solid form-wouldn’t order again, sesame chicken- surprisingly very good and the dim sum platter which they kindly made entirely in chicken. featured_reviews.review_text:
First - if you are expecting Hakka (Indian style Chinese) dishes, you may be disappointed. These are close to real Chinese food - most dishes even if mentioned spicy they are not overly spicy as Hakka dishes.

Our first time trying the Vegan Corn Curd - almost like soft silken tofu consistency. The Spicy ones were really good. The Vegan Fried Wontons and Vegan Spinach were OK. The Spinach lacked sesame seeds/oil flavour. Wontons were a bit too much doughy and less filling.

After having so many starters/appetizers, not enough space for mains. The Vegan Buddha’s Delight was better. Lots of veggies and went well with steamed rice. The Vegan Steamed Buns were a good surprise for us as we don’t normally see this in India. Well made and went well the delight as well.

featured_reviews.name: Darrell Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently dined at Stir Fry in The Gordon House, and it was an absolute delight for the palate. The menu offers a beautiful balance of bold flavors and refined textures, and every dish we tried was spot on.

We started with the Mushroom & Cheese Dumplings silky, perfectly folded parcels with just the right hint of umami. Siracha Chicken Dumplings, which packed a lively, lingering heat without overpowering the filling. The Chin Win Chicken was fragrant and well-seasoned, while the Crunchy Mushroom delivered an addictive bite that kept us reaching for more.

For mains, the Pan-fried Noodles were crisp yet delicate, soaking up the sauces beautifully. And to finish on a sweet note, the Tiramisu was indulgent but not heavy, with a balanced coffee kick.

Overall, Stir Fry combines quality ingredients with skillful execution. If you appreciate thoughtfully made Asian flavors with a modern touch, this place is well worth visiting.

featured_reviews.name: Darpan Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had booked an 11:30 pm slot through EazyDiner, but even after reaching earlier, the staff were in a tearing hurry to push through the final order — I shudder to think what would have happened had I actually arrived on time.

The Lemon Chicken Soup was bland and lifeless, the Artichoke Water Chestnut was dripping with oil, and the Edamame Truffle Dim Sum looked outright unappetising with a disturbingly artificial dirty-green hue, paired with an equally dubious-looking sauce. It’s baffling (and alarming) why such colours are being used at all.

Service was no better — they forgot our drinks, and only brought them after a reminder. To top it off, the staff dumped the main course on the table even while I was still struggling through the soup.

Overall, it was a deeply disappointing evening of bad food, rushed service, and zero finesse. Certainly not an experience I’d recommend or repeat.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had visited this restaurant many times before as it is the most popular restaurant  in South Mumbai serving the best Oriental cuisine ,but had never reviewed  it in detail.
Ambiance  is beautiful with well decorated walls,huge round tables,some with rotating centre's,& very comfortable seating .
The service is extra friendly & prompt & the servers have good knowledge  of the vast menu.
Food has always been the forte of this place,though prices are slightly on the higher side.
They serve excellent excellent cocktails & mocktails.
Tried Litchi blossom drink which was lovely.
For starters we tried their signature  Soft Corn curd which was delicious  & crispy.
Also had a Crispy prawns Cheungfun & Royal China Special Pork Ribs,which were delectable.
For mains we had  Flaming Chicken with superior  sauce & egg fried rice.
Ended our meal with their signature dessert  Chocolate dome.

featured_reviews.name: Roshani Batra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kuai Kitchen- Its a cute little beautiful place right at the busy and famous shopping street, Colaba causeway. The bright interiors, vibrant lights, chinese and panda graffitis on the walls sum up the whole little place very warm and attractive. I was literally brightened up with the ambiance the moment I entered the place. As the name suggests, it is an Asian cuisine restaurant. The service is too quick and moreover, I found the staff very friendly and educated. I had a delish food eating experience there, and so far the place has topped my list for the Asian food in Mumbai. Dimsums were too good to go for. My friend had altogether amazing experience as she was busy drinking more glasses of 'Panda Passion' - their best mocktail made of ginger and lime soda.
Menu options- Dimsum, Appetizers, Sushi, Main course available in Veg, chicken and sea food (fish/prawn) options. Here's the details on what all I had my chopsticks on -
(1) Panda Passion- Their best signature drink to go for alongwith your asian meals.
(2) Wild mushroom Dumplings- The soft and tender mushroom dumplings were damn yummy.
(3) Spicy Chicken Dumplings- Being a non veggie, I just loved this spicy chicken dumplings served in mini dimsum basket.
(4) Veg Manchurian Bao - No words to define this one.
The best and delicious bao I ever had. This has crispy manchurian filling inside with healthy veggies in the bao which was tasting too yum.
(5) Fried Spring Roll- I didn't like this appetizer. I think why beacuse we indian normally have that taste of noodles filling inside the spring roll but this didnt had the noodles; I don't know what were the fillings.
(6) Kuai Special Mixed Vegetables Soy Chilly Garlic Sauce with Steamed Rice- It is an amazing combo where the sauce is extremely stocked up with different veggies, soy, chillies and goes well with the plain steam rice.
(7) Kuai Chocolate Panda- Its the best and unique dessert to go for. Steamed bao with chocolate ganache inside tastes yummy. What else do you look for in the dessert?
I had a wonderful experience dining there. You go colaba then make sure you do visit this place for eating scenes. I love asian food; they serve amazing chinese, japanese and thai cuisine dishes although limited options but definitely the tastiest ones. I would totally recommend this place; more than that I loved their food.

featured_reviews.name: rajesh jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A casual dining space, Kuai Kitchen is the newest offering from the Royal China stable, but you never would have guessed it. Its faux-grungy interiors, complete with graffiti-splattered walls and red-and-blue accents, are a far cry from the brand’s other restaurants, including the recently launched Jia, which caters to those with fat wallets. Moreover, it is matchbox-sized in comparison to its sprawling siblings. Kuai is the kind of place where you can make a mess and still breathe easy.

While the ambience is cheerful and the menu inviting, we dropped in to check if the wallet-friendly food matches up to the standard we’re used to expecting from the brand.
we’re surprised when we spot a sushi selection on Kuai’s menu. While the absence of sashimi and nigiri is sorely missed, we’re more than happy to dig into a Volcano Prawn Tempura Roll (Rs550), which comes drizzled with mayo ‘lava’. When it arrives (really quickly, may we add), the generous portion impresses us. Digging in, however, we realise that the chef may also have been a tad generous with the salt, a problem compounded by the fact that we’ve happily dunked our roll in soy sauce. That aside, we’re thoroughly content: the tempura prawns are juicy and crunchy, and the rice wrapping is not stodgy.

featured_reviews.name: Shlok Agarwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Situated right next to HyLo in Fort, The Dimsum Room may be small in size, but it absolutely lives up to its name and concept.

This was easily one of the most enjoyable dim sum meals I’ve had in Mumbai. The creativity, flavour combinations, presentation, and execution were all on point. Every dish felt thoughtfully put together rather than just another item on a menu.

As a vegetarian, the standout dishes for me were the Cottage Cheese Cabbage Roll with Chilli Garlic Sauce and the Tofu, Shiitake & Chinese Cabbage Xiao Long Bao (soup dumplings). Both were packed with flavour, beautifully presented, and offered something a little different from the usual vegetarian dim sum options found around the city. The balance of textures and seasoning was spot on.

My wife tried the non-vegetarian selections and absolutely loved them. The Spicy Chicken & Chilli Oil dim sum was her clear favourite of the evening, even edging out the Crystal Prawn Hargow, which was excellent in its own right.

The restaurant focuses on doing one thing exceptionally well, and it shows. From the food to the presentation and overall dining experience, everything hit the right note.

A hidden gem in Fort and a must-visit for anyone who appreciates good dim sum.

featured_reviews.name: Jennifer Marawala

You’ve definitely gained regulars in us thanks to service provided by Rushab; we can’t wait to return with our family and friends.

featured_reviews.name: Jeremias Perez
featured_reviews.review_text:
Some places try to combine food, music, and atmosphere and end up doing none of them particularly well. This place somehow pulls off all three.

The cantonese inspired food was excellent. Everything we tried was balanced, flavorful, and clearly prepared with care, not just an afterthought to the music. The cocktails were equally impressive, thoughtful and beautifully executed.

But what truly sets the place apart is the listening bar. The sound system is out of this world. The speakers are extraordinary and the music experience feels immersive. The DJs were top notch as well, selecting tracks that really let the system shine.

The aesthetic ties it all together. Dark, elegant lighting, a beautiful interior, and a very deliberate atmosphere that makes you want to stay for hours. The staff were also incredibly attentive and welcoming throughout the evening.

An exceptional spot in Mumbai. If you care about sound, good cocktails, and great Cantonese food, this place is absolutely worth visiting.

Service disorganized- ginger soy for crispy prawn cheung fung barely served before waiter ran off with the rest. Dish itself was no cheung fung: just crispy prawns in rice paper, minimal sauce, disappointing size. Soupy Belgian pork dumplings average at best (meatball-like filling from frozen momos, not tender). Pork ribs tiny, stale-edged, and chewy. Inadequate air coolers made the space uncomfortably warm in Mumbai humidity- add fans/AC! Food’s forgettable, service frustrating, but view bumps it to 3 stars. Fine for a one-time scenic meal, not repeats.

Feeling under the weather, I decided to order in from Mr. Chows, Colaba, and I must say it turned out to be a comforting culinary experience. I started with their sweet corn soup, which was just the way I like it – warm, mildly seasoned, and incredibly soothing. Every spoonful brought a sense of comfort and care, perfect for someone recovering from an illness.

Along with the soup, I ordered a delicious spread: Hakka noodles, fried rice, chicken chilly , and steamed wantons. Each dish was full of flavor, well-balanced in taste, and arrived fresh and hot. The noodles had that ideal wok-tossed texture, and the fried rice was packed with just the right mix of vegetables and seasoning. The chilly chicken was tender and spicy – a definite highlight – while the steamed wantons were delicate and flavorful.

What truly stood out was the consistency and quality of the food. It felt like a warm hug on a day I truly needed it. Highly recommend Mr. Chows for anyone looking for authentic Indo-Chinese food in Colaba – whether you're unwell or just craving comfort food, they won’t disappoint!

The meat is incredibly tender and the gravy is thick, soulful, and perfectly spiced, making every bite satisfying.
The other items are equally impressive, fresh, well-cooked, and generously portioned. Despite the rush that Mohammed Ali Road is known for, the service is quick and well-managed, and the staff is polite and attentive.
Hygiene is maintained well, prices are reasonable for the quality and quantity, and the overall experience feels truly worth it. If you’re exploring Mohammed Ali Road and craving hearty, flavorful non-veg food, this place should definitely be on your list. Highly recommended!!!

featured_reviews.name: Amiit k Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing meal at Mao Family Restaurant–Best family Restaurant Kalbadevi-Best North Indian,Mughlai,Chinese,Arabian,Seafood Restaurant Kalbadevi! 😍

The Paneer Schezwan Khepsa Rice was packed with flavor, perfectly spicy, and loaded with delicious paneer pieces. The Manchurian Chatpata was crispy, tangy, and a perfect starter. The highlight was definitely the Hungama Khepsa Rice — huge portion size, rich taste, and enough to satisfy the whole group. Every bite was flavorful and satisfying.

Great food quality, generous portions, and excellent value for money. A must-visit place for Khepsa lovers in Mumbai! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

featured_reviews.name: Samruddhi Hambire
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Mao Family Restaurant for lunch and tried the Hungama Kepsa (half) — good portion size and flavorful, definitely worth it. The Chicken Tandoori was outstanding; juicy, well-marinated, and something I would surely recommend to any non-vegetarian.However, the vegetarian menu was a huge disappointment. The Paneer Kepsa tasted more like a Chinese-style gravy than authentic Kepsa, and the Paneer Crispy was neither crispy nor made from real paneer — it was clearly synthetic. At ₹265, the quantity and quality of paneer were unacceptable.In short, this place is a delight for non-vegetarians but a nightmare for vegetarians.

featured_reviews.name: Sushant Kadam
featured_reviews.review_text: Service was quick. Their speciality kepsa even half is enough for 3-4 people. The waiter suggested us hungama kepsa as their most popular kepsa. It was worth the price. Had 3 types of starters inside kepsa. Only thing is table dining arrangement is not much spacious and you need to adjust accordingly.

. Taste is best. Quantity and quality both are good.. affordable compared to other restaurants. Supportive staff .. would definitely visit again..

featured_reviews.name: Strengers Fights
featured_reviews.review_text: The food quality at Mao Restaurant is very poor. The rice is often undercooked and completely tasteless. The overall quality of the food is extremely disappointing. Even the service is not proper, and the plates and bowls do not seem properly cleaned. I would strongly advise people to avoid eating here.

featured_reviews.name: bhavika jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Mao Restaurant and had an incredible dining experience! I ordered the Chicken Noorani Kabab and Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa, and I must say, the kababs were absolutely delicious. They had a delightful tandoori coating, and the filling was made of perfectly spiced seekh chicken. The spice level was just right—medium spicy, which added to the overall flavor without overwhelming the palate.

What made it even more special was that it was served on a sizzling plate, enhancing the presentation and aroma. The Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa was a unique addition to the menu, and being the first place to serve it definitely earned them some extra points. The taste was simply amazing, and each bite was a burst of flavor.

I would highly recommend Mao Restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal. The combination of delicious food, unique offerings, and excellent presentation makes it a must-visit spot. Can't wait to go back and try more dishes!

Respected Sir/Madam,

I recently ordered food from your restaurant through a delivery service. I ordered a half plate of Chilly Kepsa, but my experience was very disappointing.

I request you to please look into this matter seriously and ensure that proper quality checks are done before sending food for delivery.

I hope you will take necessary action so that such issues do not happen again.

Thank you.

Yours sincerely,
Himanshu Gupta

featured_reviews.name: Abhilasha Akhade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I would never give the review or recommend this place to any one, On 17/04/2026, my friends and I visited the restaurant for dinner. After finishing our meal, we stepped outside and were waiting for a cab when one of my friends suddenly collapsed due to low blood pressure and fainted right outside your restaurant.

In that moment of urgency, I approached your staff requesting a small amount of sugar to help revive her. However, I was shocked by their response—they bluntly said they do not keep sugar. What was even more surprising was that at the same time, sugar was clearly available in the mukhwas kept there.

It was a matter of basic human kindness, and such a small help could have made a big difference in that situation. Unfortunately, the staff showed complete lack of empathy and humanity.

This is particularly disappointing because Kalbadevi has always been a place we frequently visit for lunch and dinner. Experiencing such insensitive behavior from your team was unexpected and unacceptable.

I do have a video of the incident, I will upload it soon. I will Raise a complaint too.

featured_reviews.name: Sumit Lalwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
visited this place last week, it is opposite to sterling cinema. It is very close to CSMT station. The place has a seating capacity of around 10-12 people indoor and outdoor.

The menu looked really appetizing, had lots of options in dim sums and momos.
I tried paneer chilli dry which was so amazing, tender paneer was loaded with flavours. The quality and quantity was amazing.

Then I tried their Japanese Udon Noodles, which are basically thick noodles made of flour. The taste was mind blowing, blended with exotic vegetables. Healthy and delicious.

Then I tried my favourite Yellow Thai curry along with steam rice. One of the best comfort foods ever. The curry was so well cooked with all the veggies, flavour was mind blowing.

Overall, an amazing experience with the food and service. Definitely going to try more options on my next visit.

featured_reviews.name: Jayadivya Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dim sum momo express i have always been a fan of their since their bandra outlet. Just love how simple the dishes are but yet so tasty and keeping up with the authenticity of the cuisine very clearly and offering you the best always. The staff is super quick in their serving and delivery. You order in and within so time the food is served hot and fresh.
The place is affordable, clean , neat, quick , offering you extensive menu giving you a wide range of options to choose from.
Must try would be
Juicy chicken tandoori momos - Juicy in the literal sense of oozing juices from the chicken filling with well done tandoori giving the smokey effect along with spicy tandoori marinate. Love the momos as they have been by far the best juicy chicken momos i have had in my life.
Crystal spicy Sriracha chicken- soft, juicy, mildly spice chicken sriracha dim sum   which just melts in your mouth and you wont regret it for sure.
Chicken nasi goreng - classic nasi goreng with juciy chicken pieces and fried egg and scrambled egg which is well tossed in sauces mildly spiced and served really hot
Thai chicken chilli basil - classic chicken chilli tossed in garlic and basil making it have a fresh and classic umami flavour with white pepper spice in the chilli chicken

Over all a 5/5 for the food, quality, quantity, value of money , taste
